abstract.para: Depending on how the system was installed, &kdump; may not be installed or enabled. Make sure it is both, so that a crash produces a dump you can analyze afterward.

step.para: Install the &kdump; package. The package pulls in kexec-tools and makedumpfile as dependencies:
Determine and, if needed, set the crash kernel memory reservation. See . The default KDUMP_CRASHKERNEL="auto" works for most systems.

If no crash kernel memory is reserved yet, kdump.service fails to start. The journal then shows No crashkernel memory reserved, Kdump cannot start. kdump-commandline.service still adds the crashkernel= values to the boot loader configuration. &kdump; starts after the reboot in the next step.
Reboot so the crash kernel memory reservation takes effect:

section.title: Installing &kdump; on the immutable variant
section.para: On the immutable variant of &productnameshort;, install and enable &kdump; through transactional-update rather than plain zypper. A plain zypper install does not fail on the read-only root file system. &zypper; transparently wraps the operation through tukit, creating a new snapshot that only takes effect after a reboot. transactional-update setup-kdump is still the recommended way to install &kdump;, since it installs, enables and calibrates the crash kernel memory reservation in a single step:

To install only the package, without the configuration steps, run transactional-update pkg install kdump and reboot. Installing only the package does not set KDUMP_UPDATE_BOOTLOADER to false or update the boot loader configuration.
To provide a custom crash kernel memory size instead of the automatically calculated one, append --crashkernel:
Reboot to activate the new snapshot and start using the updated &kdump; configuration:

note.title: /etc/sysconfig/kdump is directly editable on the immutable variant
note.para: Unlike most of the file system, /etc is its own writable subvolume on the immutable variant. Editing /etc/sysconfig/kdump directly with a text editor takes effect immediately, without needing transactional-update or a reboot, for options that do not require a new crash kernel memory reservation.

important.title: Changing the crash kernel memory reservation needs an explicit boot loader update
important.para: transactional-update setup-kdump sets KDUMP_UPDATE_BOOTLOADER="false". Unlike on a non-immutable system, kdump-commandline.service does not automatically update the boot loader on this variant even after a reboot: if the running kernel command line does not match what KDUMP_CRASHKERNEL expects, the service only logs a warning and exits with an error, leaving the old reservation in place. After editing KDUMP_CRASHKERNEL directly, push the change into the boot loader configuration explicitly:
Then reboot to activate the new snapshot. Only after this does the new crashkernel= value appear on the kernel command line.

section.title: What happens when &kdump; starts
section.para: When kdump.service starts, it rebuilds the capture initramfs if necessary and loads the capture kernel and the initramfs into the reserved memory area. Afterward, kdump-commandline.service checks whether the running kernel's command line (/proc/cmdline) contains the crashkernel= values that KDUMP_CRASHKERNEL specifies. With the default KDUMP_CRASHKERNEL="auto", these are the values that kdumptool calibrate calculates, and small differences in size are ignored. If the values are missing or different and KDUMP_UPDATE_BOOTLOADER is true (the default), kdump-commandline.service updates the boot loader configuration through pbl(8).
To check whether the service found and applied any change:
Sample output, from a system that had no crash kernel memory reserved yet:
section.screen: Oct 27 10:12:31 sles16 systemd[1]: Started Check and update kdump options on the kernel command line. Oct 27 10:12:31 sles16 kdumptool[4136]: Kdump expects these crashkernel= values on the kernel command line: Oct 27 10:12:31 sles16 kdumptool[4136]: crashkernel=72M,low crashkernel=384M,high Oct 27 10:12:31 sles16 kdumptool[4136]: (based on the output of 'kdumptool calibrate') Oct 27 10:12:31 sles16 kdumptool[4136]: No crashkernel= found in /proc/cmdline. Kdump can't be started. Oct 27 10:12:31 sles16 kdumptool[4136]: Updated the command line options in the bootloader. Oct 27 10:12:31 sles16 kdumptool[4136]: Changes will take effect on next boot. Oct 27 10:12:31 sles16 systemd[1]: kdump-commandline.service: Deactivated successfully.
section.para: If kdump-commandline.service updated the boot loader configuration, a reboot is required before the new crashkernel= values take effect and &kdump; can start capturing dumps.

important.title: Keep manual crashkernel= values out of GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX
important.para: On a system where KDUMP_UPDATE_BOOTLOADER is true, kdump-commandline.service replaces the crashkernel= values in GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT in /etc/default/grub and never changes GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX. A crashkernel= value in GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX applies to every boot entry, including the recovery entries, which otherwise carry no reservation. On the normal boot entry it then appears alongside the value the service sets, so the command line carries two conflicting reservations.
To set crashkernel= yourself, set KDUMP_UPDATE_BOOTLOADER="false" in /etc/sysconfig/kdump so the service no longer rewrites it, and put the value only in GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT.
